title: Speak what can stand accepted at the Door
summary: Guru Nanak names speech by its destination: words that bring honor are accepted, while harsh words leave the foolish mind grieving. The test of speech is whether it can stand before the Beloved.
takeaway: Speak the word that can stand accepted at the Door.
lifeApplication: Before answering, ask whether this sentence would still feel clean if it were heard at the Guru’s Door; if not, let silence answer first.

source.shortMeaning: Accepted speech is the speech that brings honor; harsh words bring grief to the foolish mind.
source.lifeApplication: Before the next sentence leaves you, measure it by the Door where honor is given.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad gives speech a spiritual test — honorable words are accepted, harsh words diminish the speaker.
evidence.turn: Move from impulse to accountability before the word leaves the mouth.
evidence.practicalImplication: Before answering, ask whether this sentence would still feel clean if it were heard at the Guru’s Door; if not, let silence answer first.
